overall_finding: Empirical CPS and NCHS scalars reproduce in saved source receipts, and the selected B packet contains the actual current diagnostic model observer and moments used by target_fit.csv. The run explicitly records empirical_target_contract_activated=false, diagnostic_only=true, production_smm_eligible=false, stationarity_certified_by_observer=false, and weights_or_standard_errors_adopted=false. Thus the legacy CPS blocked_by_age_window_mapping label is stale as a statement that no mapper exists; it remains a valid production-eligibility warning about unresolved female exposure and assumptions. The NCHS 'adapter available' wording also predates the implemented/saved period diagnostic adapter, while its population, age-tail, and stationarity qualifications remain open. This receipt makes no adoption, removal, or reweighting decision.

mapping_readout.cps_age_window: CPS women aged 40-44 are interpreted as [40,45). Four-year model cells [38,42) and [42,46) overlap by 2 and 3 years. The current uniform_birth_time mapper uses overlap weights 0.5 and 0.75 and linearly interpolates pre/post-fertility parity within each cell, with post shares 0.75 and 0.375. This is an explicit diagnostic approximation, not an exact within-age survey reconstruction.
mapping_readout.cps_population_and_denominators: The empirical rates use female CPS records and FRSUPPWT-weighted denominators. The model uses mass of one household reproductive member across model age, not a certified female exposure population; it uses endogenous model age mass, without empirical age-composition reweighting. Exactly-one is literal parity-one mass divided by all parity-positive mass, not a continuation second-birth hazard.
mapping_readout.nchs_period_and_counts: The empirical targets pool 2003-2006 first-birth counts from the US-named raw files, age/order only, with no residence filter; they are period flows, not cohort completed-fertility measures or female-age-specific rates. The model uses first-birth event-flow counts from the same stationary evaluation and takes the count-weighted age-cell midpoint or share of flow in cells starting at age 30 or above. It is not a calendar 2003-2006 dated replay.
mapping_readout.nchs_age_mapping: Both source and model use four-year midpoint classes. The source maps ages <=21 to 20, 22-25 to 24, 26-29 to 28, 30-33 to 32, 34-37 to 36, 38-41 to 40, and ages >=42 to 44. The model uses cells starting 18,22,...,42 with midpoints 20,24,...,44, and age-start >=30 for share30. Boundary classes therefore pool ages the model does not represent individually, including source ages below 18 and above 45; those are explicit approximations, not exact maternal-age support.
mapping_readout.weights: The selected B score uses frozen working minimum-distance weights. CPS weights are inverse squared pooled correlation-one candidate SEs derived from annual official approximate Census GVFs with observed annual bases held fixed; this is not a design-exact pooled SE, and cross-year covariance/random-ratio-base uncertainty is not certified. NCHS has no probability-sample SE; its weights use 2003-2006 annual temporal SD as a typical-year discrepancy scale, not sampling uncertainty. These are experimental score inputs; the saved run says the empirical target contract and weights are not activated as production SMM inputs.
